 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To
Declare That The Scheme Of Acquisition, As Notified
Vide Final Notification Dtd 27.05.1997 Issued Under
Section 28(4) Of The Kiadb Act, Vide Annx-B, As Having
Lapsed In So Far As The Petitioners Holding In Survey
Number 126/2P8, Survey Numbers 126/2P6 And Survey
No.126/2P7 Measuring Extents Of 48 Cents, 30 Cents
And 40 Cents Respectively, Of Tokur Village,
Mangalore Taluk, In Terms Of Section 24(2) Of The
Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land
Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act,
2013 Or In The Alternative And Etc.,
 This Petition Coming On For Orders This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioners are knocking at the doors of Writ Court seeking to lay a challenge to the acquisition of their land pursuant to the proceedings taken up under Section 28 of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 on the ground that the proceedings have lapsed in the light of Section 24(2)
Sandeep Shenoy vs State Of Karnataka on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24020256/
2 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Rehabilitation Act, 2013.
2. Learned AGA appearing for the State and Panel Counsel for the KIADB, oppose the petition contending that in view of the decision of the Apex Court in LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER VS.
ANASUYA BAI (2017) 3 SCC 313, the benefit of lapse as envisaged u/s 24(2) does not avail to acquisitions done under statutes other than Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
3.

sentences.text: They further contend that the scheme of acquisition under the provisions of 1966 Act is a bit in variance with that of the erstwhile 1894 Act in the sense in case of the former, land immediately vests in the State on issuance of the Final Notification u/s 28(4) of the 1966 Act, notwithstanding the award being passed or compensation being paid vide Division Bench judgment in W.P.No.17600/2004 between NANDI INFRASTRUCTURE CORRIDOR ENTERPRISE LIMITED vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA, disposed off on 15.06.2011.

entities.text: NANDI INFRASTRUCTURE CORRIDOR ENTERPRISE LIMITED vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court broadly being in agreement with the submission made on behalf of the respondents, declines indulgence in the matter.
In the above circumstances, Writ Petition is dismissed, costs having been made easy.
